about: Ola's worked examples (OLA-181): app requests that ended well, shown to the model when a new request is close to one. Test requests only, written for this library: none is one of the seven measured problems in evals/apps/problems.json, so the measure is not taught to the test. Bart's own kept requests are added on the Ola machine from a file outside the repo (OLA_EXAMPLES_EXTRA). Each one: request, tags (kind words), asked (what it plainly means, one line each), built, tried (each item tried on the page, with what was seen), answer.

examples.request: make me a reading list app where each book has a rating and I can mark books as finished
asked: a field for the title and a button to add a book; the book shows in the list right away
each book has a rating: 1 to 5 stars shown beside that book, and it can be changed
each book can be marked finished, and finished books look different (struck through, or under Finished)
the list is still there after the page is reloaded (saved in localStorage)
an empty list says so instead of showing nothing
built: one folder: index.html, style.css, app.js; no server, no outside files
app.js keeps an array of {id, title, rating, finished} in localStorage under one key, reads it at start, writes it after every change, and redraws the whole list from it
the rating is five buttons per book with aria-label 'Rate 1' to 'Rate 5'; the chosen number also shows as text ('4 of 5') so it can be read
Enter in the title field adds the book too
tried: ola-page index.html --out .shots/try.png --do "fill 1=Parable of the Sower" --do "click Add" --text: the list showed 'Parable of the Sower'
then --do "click Rate 4" --text: '4 of 5' showed beside that book, and the picture showed four filled stars
then --do "click Finished" --text: the book moved under 'Finished' and was struck through
opened the page again with no steps (a reload): the book, its rating and its finished state were still there
cleared localStorage and opened it: 'No books yet' showed
examples.answer: Named each of the five items and what was seen when it was tried, said where the list is saved (this browser only), and how to open the page.

examples.request: make a stopwatch page with lap times for our relay race practice
asked: a big time display that starts at 00:00.00
Start makes the time move while it runs; Stop holds it; Reset goes back to 00:00.00
Lap records the time at that moment in a list, newest first, numbered
it keeps correct time even if the tab is slow (time from Date.now(), not a counter of ticks)
built: index.html, style.css, app.js; the display is one element with tabular numbers so it does not jump
app.js stores the start moment and the time already run; every 50 ms (requestAnimationFrame when visible) it shows now - start + already run
Lap pushes the current reading; the list shows 'Lap 3  01:12.40' and the gap from the lap before
tried: ola-page index.html --out .shots/a.png --do "click Start" --wait 500 --text, then the same with --wait 3000: the time read about 00:00.5 and then about 00:03.0, so it moves
--do "click Start" --wait 1500 --do "click Lap" --text: 'Lap 1' showed with about 00:01.5
--do "click Start" --wait 1000 --do "click Stop" looked twice with --wait 500 and --wait 2000: the same reading both times, so Stop holds
then --do "click Reset" --text: 00:00.00 and the laps list empty
examples.answer: Listed Start, Stop, Reset and Lap with the readings seen when each was tried, and how to open the page.

examples.request: build a recipe scaler: I paste ingredients with amounts and pick how many servings, and it gives the new amounts
asked: a box to paste ingredients, one per line, like '2 cups flour' or '1/2 tsp salt'
a field for the servings the recipe makes and a field for the servings wanted
the new amounts, one per line, right for fractions and mixed numbers (1 1/2), shown as kitchen fractions
lines with no number are kept as they are
built: index.html, app.js; the parser reads a leading number in the forms 2, 2.5, 1/2 and 1 1/2, multiplies by wanted / makes, and prints the result rounded to the nearest 1/8 as a fraction
the result updates on every change of any field (input events), with no button needed; a Scale button is there too for people who look for one
tried: known answers first: ola-page index.html --do "fill 1=2 cups flour" --do "fill 2=4" --do "fill 3=8" --text: '4 cups flour' (2 doubled is 4)
--do "fill 1=1 1/2 tsp salt" --do "fill 2=4" --do "fill 3=2" --text: '3/4 tsp salt' (half of one and a half)
--do "fill 1=salt to taste" --text: 'salt to taste' unchanged
an empty servings field: a short message instead of NaN
examples.answer: Gave the three worked numbers and their results, so the person can see the math is right, and said which formats are understood.

examples.request: make a tic tac toe game for two players on one screen
asked: a 3 by 3 board shows when the page opens, all empty
players take turns: the first click puts X, the next O, and a taken square cannot be changed
three in a row (row, column or diagonal) says who won and stops the game; a full board with no line says it is a draw
whose turn it is shows above the board; New game clears it
built: index.html, style.css, app.js; the board is nine <button> elements in a CSS grid (aria-label 'square 1' to 'square 9'), so it is drawn by the page, not on a canvas
app.js holds the nine cells in an array and checks the eight lines after every move
tried: ola-page index.html --out .shots/start.png --text: nine empty squares in the picture and 'X to play'
--do "click square 1" --do "click square 4" --do "click square 2" --do "click square 5" --do "click square 3" --text: 'X wins' and the squares no longer respond
--do "click square 1" --do "click square 1" --text: square 1 stayed X and it was still O's turn
played a draw (1,2,3 by X,O,X then 5,4,6,8,7,9): 'Draw'
examples.answer: Described the board, the turns, the win and the draw as tried, with the picture of the opening board.

examples.request: make an event page for our tenants union meeting on Thursday January 21, 2027 at 6:30pm at the library, where people can RSVP and share the link
asked: the event's name, the date as written (Thursday, January 21, 2027, 6:30 pm) and the place, first on the page
an RSVP: a name field and a button; the name shows in a list of who is coming, and the list is still there after a reload (this browser only, said on the page)
a Share button: on a phone it opens the phone's share sheet (navigator.share), elsewhere it copies the page's address and says 'Link copied'
the date is checked: January 21, 2027 is a Thursday
built: used the designer skill for the page itself (one headline, the facts, one action)
index.html, style.css, app.js; RSVPs in localStorage; Share uses navigator.share when it exists and navigator.clipboard.writeText(location.href) otherwise, with a visible message either way
tried: python3 -c 'import datetime; print(datetime.date(2027,1,21).strftime("%A"))' printed Thursday
ola-page index.html --out .shots/page.png --text: the name, 'Thursday, January 21, 2027, 6:30 pm' and the library were the first words
--do "fill 1=Rosa" --do "click RSVP" --text: 'Rosa' under 'Who is coming (1)'; opened again: still there
--do "click Share" --text: 'Link copied' showed (the headless browser has no share sheet, so the copy path ran)
examples.answer: Said what each part did when tried, that RSVPs are kept only in each visitor's own browser (a shared list needs a server or a form service), and how to publish the page if they want a link.

examples.request: build a word scramble game that uses ai to make new words on any theme
asked: a theme field and a button that makes a new round of words for that theme
each word shows scrambled, with a box to type the answer; a right answer is marked right, a wrong one says try again
it works when no AI can be reached: a built-in list of words per common theme, and the page says it used the built-in list
the AI part is real: a small server that asks a model for words as JSON, and the page uses it when it is running
built: index.html, app.js for the game; server.mjs (Node, no packages) with one route, GET /api/words?theme=..., that asks a model for 8 words as JSON and checks the reply before passing it on; the key is read from an environment variable and never written into a file
app.js tries /api/words first with a 6 second limit; on any failure or a bad reply it uses words.json, the built-in lists, and shows 'Using the built-in words (no AI connected)'
the game itself never depends on the AI: scrambling, checking and the score are plain code
tried: ola-page index.html --do "fill theme=animals" --do "click New words" --text: 8 scrambled words and 'Using the built-in words', since nothing serves /api/words here
unscrambled the first word by reading words.json, then --do "fill 2=<that word>" --do "press Enter" --text: 'Right' and the score went to 1
--do "fill 2=zzz" --do "press Enter" --text: 'Try again'
node server.mjs with a stand-in model reply (a local file) and curl 127.0.0.1:8787/api/words?theme=ocean: 8 words as JSON
examples.answer: Said plainly that the game works now with built-in words and that the AI words need server.mjs running with a model key, with the one command to start it; named each thing tried and what was seen.

examples.request: make a page where our group can enter shared expenses and see who owes who
asked: add a person's name; add an expense with who paid, how much and what for
a list of the expenses and the total
who owes who: the fewest payments that settle everyone, in dollars and cents
kept after a reload (this browser only)
built: index.html, app.js; amounts kept in cents as whole numbers so 10.00 / 3 never prints 3.3333; the settle step pairs the largest debtor with the largest creditor until all are at zero
tried: known answer: Ana paid 30.00, Ben paid 0, Chi paid 0 (fill and click Add each); --text showed 'Ben owes Ana $10.00' and 'Chi owes Ana $10.00'
an amount of 10 split three ways: the shares added back up to exactly $10.00 (3.34 + 3.33 + 3.33)
a letter typed as the amount: 'Enter an amount like 12.50', nothing added
opened again: the people and expenses were still there
examples.answer: Showed the worked case with its result so the math can be checked, and said where the data is kept.

examples.request: make flashcards for studying Spanish verbs, where I can add my own cards and it shows my score
asked: a card shows one side (the Spanish verb); Show answer reveals the other side
I got it / Missed it buttons move to the next card and count the score ('3 of 5 right')
a form to add my own card (front and back); it joins the deck at once and is kept after a reload
starts with a few real cards so it is not empty
built: index.html, style.css, app.js; the deck in localStorage, seeded with ten common verbs (hablar, comer, vivir…) the first time
the answer side is hidden with the hidden attribute until Show answer, so it is not in the page's text before then
tried: ola-page index.html --text: one Spanish verb showed and its English did not
--do "click Show answer" --text: the English showed
--do "click Show answer" --do "click I got it" --do "click Show answer" --do "click Missed it" --text: '1 of 2 right' and a third card
--do "fill front=correr" --do "fill back=to run" --do "click Add card", then opened again: 'correr' was in the deck
examples.answer: Named each part and what was seen, and how to add cards.
